deps: V8: cherry-pick 786c1c2d88d4

Original commit message:

    [stack-traces] Fix overflow in Error.stackTraceLimit trimming

    When stack traces are captured for uncaught exceptions (enabled via
    Isolate::SetCaptureStackTraceForUncaughtExceptions, e.g. by the
    inspector or by Node.js's --trace-uncaught), CaptureAndSetErrorStack
    reuses the simple stack trace and trims it to Error.stackTraceLimit.

    Error.stackTraceLimit counts frames, but the raw call site data stores
    CallSiteInfo::Fields::kCount slots per frame, so the trim multiplied the
    limit by kCount: once in the uint32_t comparison against the array
    length and once, as int, to compute the new length. GetStackTraceLimit
    clamps the limit to [0, INT_MAX], so for very large limits the uint32_t
    product can wrap to a value below the array length. The trim branch is
    then taken although the limit exceeds the number of captured frames,
    and the int multiplication of the new length overflows.

    On main (kCount == 5) the product first wraps at 858993460. That limit
    trimmed the raw data to 4 slots (no complete frame) and 858993461 to 9
    slots (one frame), so error.stack silently lost frames. Infinity, the
    value from the Node.js report, is clamped to INT_MAX; its wrapped
    product (2147483643) is not below the array length, so on main it does
    not take the trim branch and does not reach the signed overflow.

    Fix this by comparing the limit with the number of frames in the raw
    data (length / kCount), and only multiplying once the limit is known to
    be smaller than the frame count. The resulting length is then bounded
    by the existing array length and cannot overflow. Behavior for limits
    that did not overflow is unchanged, since the raw data length is always
    a multiple of kCount.

    This regressed with https://crrev.com/c/7673818 (ebd15783b7b,
    "[objects]: Defer CallSiteInfo creation"), which switched from one
    CallSiteInfo per frame to kCount raw slots per frame.

    This is the underlying cause of Node.js issue 66074. The symptom there
    differs from main: Node's V8 14.6 backport of that change has
    kCount == 6 and uses int for the comparison and for RightTrim, so the
    product overflows for limits above 357913941. For many of those,
    including Infinity (INT_MAX * 6 wraps to -6), the result is negative
    and fails "Check failed: new_capacity > 0." in RightTrim. Comparing in
    frames avoids the overflow in both cases.

    The new cctest CaptureStackTraceForUncaughtExceptionHugeStackTraceLimit
    enables capture for uncaught exceptions and checks that limits of
    858993460, 858993461 and Infinity yield the same error.stack as a limit
    of 10, and that a limit of 1 still trims to a single frame. 858993460
    and 858993461 are the first limits whose product with kCount wraps
    around uint32_t; both fail without this change. The new test and the

Original commit message:

    [torque] Fix C++ object layout assertions for MSVC STL

    The assertions generated for @cppObjectLayoutDefinition classes assume
    that the first field of a derived class starts at sizeof(Parent) and
    that sizeof(Class) == the packed size computed by Torque. Both
    assumptions break when compiling with the MSVC STL, which stores
    std::atomic<T> with alignas(sizeof(T)). Under the Microsoft C++ ABI an
    alignas() is a required alignment that #pragma pack cannot lower, so the
    std::atomic bit fields of Map force Map, and in turn the pack(1)
    ExtendedMap, to align by 4 bytes. After rounding up,

    sizeof(ExtendedMap) == sizeof(Map) + 4 == kSize + 3

    so

    static_assert(kSize == sizeof(ExtendedMap))

    fails. The base subobject size is not rounded up
    however, so JSInterceptorMap places its first field at sizeof(Map) + 1
    rather than sizeof(ExtendedMap), and

    static_assert(kFlagsOffset == offsetof(JSInterceptorMap, flags_))

    fails as well.

    Fix this by:

    - Using the packed parent size that Torque already knows as the offset
      of the first derived field instead of sizeof(Parent).
    - Relaxing the assertion to only require that sizeof(Class) does not
      exceed kSize by alignof(Class) or more, so that any extra bytes fit
      into the alignment padding.

crypto: isolate provider EC PKCS8 encoding

OpenSSL's provider ec_pki_priv_to_der() temporarily changes EC_KEY
encoding flags on the input key. Concurrent PKCS8 exports can emit
inconsistent DER or affect a concurrent SEC1 export. The old Node key
mutex never covered this path.

encoding flags, point conversion form, parameters, and provider.
Legacy OpenSSL and BoringSSL already encode using local flags.

Restore concurrent KeyObject PKCS8 DER assertions and cover PEM and
SEC1 exports, including ECPrivateKey inputs without a public point.

crypto: remove key export and metadata locks

Raw and JWK getters return independently owned bytes or BIGNUMs. RSA
metadata snapshots public parameters and PSS restrictions. EC fallback
paths reconstruct or duplicate the source key. EC PKCS8 export changes
encoding flags only on its own clone.

Early OpenSSL 3 key downgrading mutated shared provider fields. Current
OpenSSL publishes separate legacy and provider conversion caches under
internal read/write locks. Ordinary DER/PEM export, equality, signing,
and key derivation already access the same keys without these locks.

Remove export and metadata acquisitions, including their coverage of V8
allocation and encoding, and remove the now-unused shared mutex storage.
Retain shared immutable key ownership. The concurrent reuse test checks
that EC PKCS8 export leaves the original flags intact.

ncrypto::KEM creates a new EVP_PKEY_CTX per operation. Parameters,
entropy, scratch buffers, and outputs are private to each call. ML-KEM
expansion finishes during import, and operations read an immutable key.
EC and X25519 retain read-only recipient keys. RSA synchronizes mutable
caches internally.

CryptoKey. Cover cold keys and worker clones across RSA, EC, X25519, and

RSA_Cipher delegates to ncrypto::Rsa with a new EVP_PKEY_CTX per
operation. Padding, digests, labels, and output buffers belong to that
context. OpenSSL and BoringSSL synchronize RSA blinding and Montgomery
caches internally.

cache under its own lock.

Secret key bytes are immutable after KeyObjectData construction. AES,

The ngtcp2 and nghttp3 allocators shared one thread_local state whose
BindingData pointer was set by the last BindingData that handed out an
allocator. With several Environments on a thread, memory allocated for

http: add websocketMask() and websocketUnmask()

Add websocketMask(source, mask, output[, offset[, length]]) and
websocketUnmask(buffer, mask), which XOR data with a repeating 4-byte
key. This is the masking that WebSocket clients apply to every frame
they send (RFC 6455, Section 5.3), and that servers undo on every frame
they receive.

Userland WebSocket implementations do this either with a byte-by-byte
JS loop (undici, and ws without optional dependencies) or with the
bufferutil native addon. bufferutil is installed for only about 3% of
ws downloads and has no linux-arm64 prebuild, so almost all users run
the JS loop. The signature matches bufferutil, so existing users can
switch with a feature check, as ws did for buffer.isUtf8().

The implementation uses a V8 fast API call and processes 8-byte words,
which the compiler vectorizes. It handles overlapping source and output
views, and treats every view type as raw bytes. It is about 20x faster
than the JS loop at 1 KiB and 40x faster at 64 KiB, and faster than
bufferutil at every size from 32 bytes up.

    According to the spec, TypedArray.prototype.set checks
    IsImmutableBuffer(target.[[ViewedArrayBuffer]]) before converting
    the offset argument to integer and before reading from the source
    object.

    Additionally, when setting from a TypedArray source, reading from an
    immutable source TypedArray is permitted, so the source array should
    be validated using TypedArrayAccessMode::kRead rather than kWrite.

    Drive-By: Add a fast case for Smi indices where the steps are not
              observable and we can fold all checks.

commit.message:
deps: V8: cherry-pick 786c1c2d88d4

Original commit message:

    [stack-traces] Fix overflow in Error.stackTraceLimit trimming

    When stack traces are captured for uncaught exceptions (enabled via
    Isolate::SetCaptureStackTraceForUncaughtExceptions, e.g. by the
    inspector or by Node.js's --trace-uncaught), CaptureAndSetErrorStack
    reuses the simple stack trace and trims it to Error.stackTraceLimit.

    Error.stackTraceLimit counts frames, but the raw call site data stores
    CallSiteInfo::Fields::kCount slots per frame, so the trim multiplied the
    limit by kCount: once in the uint32_t comparison against the array
    length and once, as int, to compute the new length. GetStackTraceLimit
    clamps the limit to [0, INT_MAX], so for very large limits the uint32_t
    product can wrap to a value below the array length. The trim branch is
    then taken although the limit exceeds the number of captured frames,
    and the int multiplication of the new length overflows.

    On main (kCount == 5) the product first wraps at 858993460. That limit
    trimmed the raw data to 4 slots (no complete frame) and 858993461 to 9
    slots (one frame), so error.stack silently lost frames. Infinity, the
    value from the Node.js report, is clamped to INT_MAX; its wrapped
    product (2147483643) is not below the array length, so on main it does
    not take the trim branch and does not reach the signed overflow.

    Fix this by comparing the limit with the number of frames in the raw
    data (length / kCount), and only multiplying once the limit is known to
    be smaller than the frame count. The resulting length is then bounded
    by the existing array length and cannot overflow. Behavior for limits
    that did not overflow is unchanged, since the raw data length is always
    a multiple of kCount.

    This regressed with https://crrev.com/c/7673818 (ebd15783b7b,
    "[objects]: Defer CallSiteInfo creation"), which switched from one
    CallSiteInfo per frame to kCount raw slots per frame.

    This is the underlying cause of Node.js issue 66074. The symptom there
    differs from main: Node's V8 14.6 backport of that change has
    kCount == 6 and uses int for the comparison and for RightTrim, so the
    product overflows for limits above 357913941. For many of those,
    including Infinity (INT_MAX * 6 wraps to -6), the result is negative
    and fails "Check failed: new_capacity > 0." in RightTrim. Comparing in
    frames avoids the overflow in both cases.

    The new cctest CaptureStackTraceForUncaughtExceptionHugeStackTraceLimit
    enables capture for uncaught exceptions and checks that limits of
    858993460, 858993461 and Infinity yield the same error.stack as a limit
    of 10, and that a limit of 1 still trims to a single frame. 858993460
    and 858993461 are the first limits whose product with kCount wraps
    around uint32_t; both fail without this change. The new test and the
    existing stack trace tests also pass in a UBSan build, with no
    diagnostics.

    Bug: 565047704

commit.message:
deps: V8: cherry-pick 5404e0f85a83

Original commit message:

    [cppgc] Use _AddressOfReturnAddress() for StackStartMarker under MSVC

    include/cppgc/heap.h is a public header, and since b3cb54c7e65
    ("[heap] Add StackStartMarker for cppgc") it calls
    __builtin_frame_address(0) unconditionally. That builtin does not exist
    in MSVC, so any translation unit built with cl.exe that includes the
    header (directly or through v8-cppgc.h) fails to compile, even if it
    never constructs a StackStartMarker.

    Use _AddressOfReturnAddress() when V8_CC_MSVC is set, which is what
    base::Stack::GetCurrentStackPosition() already does for the same
    purpose, and keep __builtin_frame_address(0) elsewhere.

    Bug: none

commit.message:
deps: V8: cherry-pick 99ebeac9c548

Original commit message:

    [torque] Fix C++ object layout assertions for MSVC STL

    The assertions generated for @cppObjectLayoutDefinition classes assume
    that the first field of a derived class starts at sizeof(Parent) and
    that sizeof(Class) == the packed size computed by Torque. Both
    assumptions break when compiling with the MSVC STL, which stores
    std::atomic<T> with alignas(sizeof(T)). Under the Microsoft C++ ABI an
    alignas() is a required alignment that #pragma pack cannot lower, so the
    std::atomic bit fields of Map force Map, and in turn the pack(1)
    ExtendedMap, to align by 4 bytes. After rounding up,

    sizeof(ExtendedMap) == sizeof(Map) + 4 == kSize + 3

    so

    static_assert(kSize == sizeof(ExtendedMap))

    fails. The base subobject size is not rounded up
    however, so JSInterceptorMap places its first field at sizeof(Map) + 1
    rather than sizeof(ExtendedMap), and

    static_assert(kFlagsOffset == offsetof(JSInterceptorMap, flags_))

    fails as well.

    Fix this by:

    - Using the packed parent size that Torque already knows as the offset
      of the first derived field instead of sizeof(Parent).
    - Relaxing the assertion to only require that sizeof(Class) does not
      exceed kSize by alignof(Class) or more, so that any extra bytes fit
      into the alignment padding.

    Co-Authored-By: StefanStojanovic <stefan.stojanovic@janeasystems.com>
    Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/65161

Original commit message:

    [platform][posix] Fallback to conservative stack limit on musl

    For most libcs, pthread_getattr_np() returns the the stack reserved
    limit on the main thread, but musl only returns the current high-water
    mark at the time of the call. There's no macro to detect musl, so just
    fallback to the conservative stack limit in cases where the libc is
    not one that is known to work.

    Refs: https://github.com/nodejs/node/pull/65161

commit.message:
build: use ICU_UTIL_DATA_STATIC across V8

ICU_UTIL_DATA_SHARED had been removed since
https://crrev.com/c/1513615, but Node.js still defined
it and relied on the removed path on Windows, so the ICU
initialization in mksnapshot had been silently failing
since then. https://crrev.com/c/7679153 made the failure
visible so the build started breaking on Windows. Fix it
by always using ICU_UTIL_DATA_STATIC since we already compile
the ICU data statically in.

When a BYOK model's first call in a user turn finished with no visible
output (no non-whitespace text, no tool calls, no reasoning summary), the
BYOK proxy sent the Copilot runtime a valid, empty Responses completion.
The runtime then failed the turn with the generic "No response was
returned. Send your message again to retry." error, and the reason was
lost.

The proxy now detects this case, logs the session, model, and output item
types, and returns a descriptive 422 error that the runtime shows as-is
and does not retry. Empty responses later in a turn (after tool results)
still pass through, because the runtime completes those turns normally.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
mcp: show where built-in MCP servers come from

The Chat Customizations MCP details page showed no source for built-in
servers: the header fell back to a literal "mcp.json" and the
Configuration section was empty without explanation.

- Forward the runtime-reported display name and source plugin from the
  Copilot agent host as namespaced customization metadata.
- Show where a server comes from when it has no configuration file
  (e.g. "Built-in: Copilot", "Managed by Copilot", "Agent host
  configuration"); Copilot-contributed servers link to their extension.
- Explain why the agent's own servers have no definition, and link
  github-mcp-server to chat.agentHost.githubMcpServer.enabled.
- Show the definition of servers added to the agent host configuration
  and group them under User.
- Add Show Extension / Show Configuration to built-in row menus.

Fixes #338719

commit.message:
agentHost: degrade BYOK input_file parts instead of failing the turn

The Copilot runtime sends document attachments (e.g. a referenced PDF) as
Responses `input_file` parts. The BYOK loopback proxy only translated text and
image parts, so these turns failed with `400 Unsupported input[N].content[M]
type 'input_file'`. BYOK models are served through the LM API, which has no
capability declaring document input, so replace the file with a note telling
the model it was omitted.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
chat: Enrich reference previews and add pill context copying (#339342)

* chat: Enrich reference previews and add pill context copying

Resolve GitHub reference metadata on demand without promoting references to authored artifacts. Prefetch a bounded initial set, preserve hover intent through updates, and share copy actions with pill context menus. Replace isolated hover galleries with interactive reference fixtures and deterministic rich-preview captures.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Harden lazy reference resolution and cache retention

Address Copilot review by validating canonical reference numbers, evicting metadata and hover descriptors no longer referenced, preserving resolved titles during checks enrichment, and treating checks failures as optional. Cover eviction races and partial failures with targeted tests.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Stabilize visible reference fetching and checks enrichment

Notify only newly visible rows after layout settles, preserve reference identity during scroll updates, and resolve PR core before subscribing to head-specific checks. Use URLs after metadata failure and update the toolbar test harness for its GitHub service dependency.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Format lazy reference regression coverage

Apply the repository formatter after the review and CI fixes.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Cancel evicted GitHub reference requests

Give each lazy resolution its own abort scope and cancel credential acquisition and resource refreshes when references are removed, sessions change, accounts change, or the resolver is disposed.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Preserve reference dropdown scroll position during updates

Keep the viewport stable when asynchronously resolved metadata rebuilds the dropdown, rather than revealing its previously focused row.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Discard canceled metadata and scope fixture hover routing

Do not publish stale results after reference eviction, account changes or disposal. Preserve cancellation through optional checks and validate both rejecting and resolving canceled requests. Register base hover routing only while reference fixtures are mounted and restore the previous delegate afterward.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Preserve resource previews during reference metadata updates

Reuse image and location hover content by stable entry identity while keeping actions current, disposing replaced or removed resources. Forward fixture fallback hover methods explicitly so prototype methods retain their receiver.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Validate reference hosts and seed scroll prefetch visibility

Reject enterprise credentials for public GitHub references before subscribing. Seed the initial visible row identities so a small first scroll does not retry failed initial prefetches. Cover both behaviors and use realistic API hosts in mocks.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Complete visible reference prefetch without duplicate retries

Track prefetch attempts per dropdown opening so the first scroll can resolve initially visible entries beyond the first five without retrying that initial batch. Avoid repeating URLs in accessible descriptions when the visible fallback label already contains the URL.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

---------

commit.message:
agentHost: retire legacy sandbox policy enforcement (#339396)

## Summary

Retire legacy VS Code sandbox policies from the Copilot Agent Host
policy contract and roll back the mandatory legacy sandbox requirement
added by #339144. Enterprise sandbox enforcement in Agent Host should
use [Copilot managed
settings](https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/administer-copilot/manage-for-enterprise/use-managed-settings/get-started),
not migration of the old preview device policies.

- Remove the connection-owned legacy sandbox requirement, while
retaining native managed sandbox enforcement and the later
session-restoration/reconciliation fixes.
- Mark nine legacy sandbox settings deprecated, keep their migration
notices visible, and preserve their defaults. Add deprecation and
replacement guidance to the four device-policy descriptions and
generated catalog.
- Classify those four retired policies as `notApplicable`, rather than
outstanding Agent Host parity gaps. Update diagnostics, tests, and
contributor documentation together. New Agent Host sandbox controls are
not deprecated.

## Admin and user impact

**`ChatAgentSandboxEnabled: on` no longer guarantees sandboxing in Agent
Host.** Existing setting forwarding remains, so it can supply an On
default, but a session Off selection can override it.

To require sandboxing in Copilot Agent Host, use native managed
`sandbox.enabled: true`. Use `sandbox.allowBypass: false` when bypass
must be prohibited. Outbound network restrictions use
`sandbox.userPolicy.network.allowOutbound`.

Local harness behavior is unchanged. Native managed restrictions,
permitted-bypass controls, restored-session reconciliation, and other
legacy permission translations remain intact. `notApplicable` records
the retirement of the legacy policy contract; it does not mean forwarded
settings have no effect or certify enforcement parity.

The deprecated device policies are `ChatAgentSandboxEnabled`,
`ChatAgentSandboxAllowNetwork`,
`ChatAgentSandboxAllowUnsandboxedCommands`, and
`ChatAgentSandboxAllowAutoApprove`.

## Validation

- Rebased onto current `main`; core compilation completed with zero
errors.
- 528 focused tests passed, covering native sandbox enforcement,
restoration, bypass/fail-closed behavior, ordinary forwarding,
connection lifecycle, deprecation metadata, catalog classifications, and
diagnostics.
- A test-only follow-up fixes two stale CI expectations. Both failures
were reproduced locally, then the affected suites passed 69 tests in
Electron and 68 in WebKit, including unchanged Local/Copilot rollout
selection.
- Targeted hygiene and whitespace checks passed.
- Canonical Workbench and Agents policy-export check passed.

Live MDM deployment was not exercised. Release notes and sandbox
migration guidance have also been updated locally in `vscode-docs` for
separate publication.

*🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*

test: align legacy sandbox retirement expectations

Keep rollout-selection coverage for all four retired sandbox policies while expecting no readiness gaps. Update the Settings editor renderer assertion for the completed deprecation notice without changing product behavior.

Don't treat a failed GitHub session lookup as a sign-out (#339393)

Refreshing the default account can hit a session lookup error while the
GitHub authentication provider is briefly unavailable, for example when
the extension host restarts to apply managed telemetry policy. That error
was handled like a sign-out: the account was cleared and, with
forceRemoteSettingsRefresh, the managed settings gate blocked AI and asked
a signed-in user to sign in.

Keep the account that is already known for the same provider, with its
policy and managed settings freshness, when the lookup fails. Session
removals still clear the account, and a failed lookup before any account
is known still reports a missing token.

commit.message:
sessions: Add compact layout density to the Agents window (#339353)

<!-- Thank you for submitting a Pull Request. Please:
* Read our Pull Request guidelines:

https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/wiki/How-to-Contribute#pull-requests
* Associate an issue with the Pull Request.
* Ensure that the code is up-to-date with the `main` branch.
* Include a description of the proposed changes and how to test them.
-->

## Summary

Bring `window.density.layout` to the Agents window, independently of the
editor-window Modern UI setting.

- Make Compact panels meet edge-to-edge, retaining visible single
separators and continuous connected-tab outlines.
- Keep tab/action-area horizontal padding consistent between densities.
- Use a 44px title bar in Default and 35px in Compact; preserve control
sizes, update auxiliary layouts and notification offsets, and improve
native macOS/right-hand action spacing.
- Keep density-menu changes local to the Agents window and accurately
display inherited User values. Preserve explicit empty array overrides
when editing inherited settings.
- Keep macOS traffic-light horizontal positioning fixed across
densities, while preserving OS-version-specific vertical centering and
zoom behavior.
- Ensure built-in themes provide visible Agents panel borders.

## Before / after

Captured in the same 1440 × 900 Chromium viewport with Dark 2026, the
desktop Agents layout, a Search editor and the bottom panel open.
Authentication, filesystem and terminal use the existing test mocks; no
live agent requests or user workspace data are involved. Before is the
branch's main merge-base (`3bf9306bd0d`); after is the final branch.

| Before | After — Default | After — Compact |
| --- | --- | --- |
| ![Before: main, 35px title bar and floating panel
gaps](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/aca23716-0404-45be-ac71-d6362b3c8fee)
| ![After: Default, 44px title bar and visible panel
borders](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d0ae3923-da42-4887-b4d2-8629c6ab8b59)
| ![After: Compact, 35px title bar and zero gaps between
panels](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/5b796465-71cb-4a00-a48e-9ab3c3a80375)
|

## How to test

1. Open the Agents window and use **View > Layout Density** (also
available from the title-bar context menu).
2. Switch between Default and Compact without reloading. Default has
floating gaps and a taller title bar; Compact has no inter-panel gaps.
Tab outlines and action sizes should stay intact.
3. Change `window.density.layout` in User and Agents Window Settings.
Verify the Agents override wins, User settings stay unchanged, and
removing the override restores inheritance after reload.
4. Clear an inherited array setting in Agents Window Settings. An
explicit `[]` must persist; **Reset Setting** must restore inheritance.
5. Check panels and connected tabs in the built-in dark, light and
high-contrast themes.

## Validation

- `npm run typecheck-client` — passed.
- The focused Chromium command below — 452 passed, 1 existing
native-only frosted-glass test skipped.
- `npm run test-node -- --run
src/vs/sessions/test/node/builtinThemeBorders.test.ts --reporter dot` —
passed; checks all 19 built-in color themes and their inherited border
values.
- `npm run valid-layers-check` — passed.
- `git diff --check` — passed.
- Before/after DOM measurements — Default title bar 44px; Compact 35px,
with 0px horizontal/vertical inter-panel gaps and 0px outer grid
gutters.
- Isolated source-method probe of the renderer/native traffic-light
positioning path — passed for pre-Tahoe and Tahoe+, at zoom factors 0.8,
1 and 1.25.

npm run test-browser-no-install -- --browser chromium --reporter dot \

  --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/workbench.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/titlebarPart.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/layoutActions.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/chatCompositeBar.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/test/browser/editorPart.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/editor/test/browser/editor.contribution.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/services/configuration/test/browser/configurationService.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/sessions/contrib/chat/test/browser/sessionsChatAccessibilityHelp.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/preferences/test/browser/settingsTree.test.ts \
  --run src/vs/workbench/contrib/preferences/test/browser/settingsTreeModels.test.ts \

commit.message:
chat: Fail requests whose selected model is unavailable (#339307)

* chat: Fail requests whose selected model is unavailable

A selected model the extension host couldn't resolve silently fell back to the default (Auto) model, so requests were answered and billed by a different model than the one shown in the picker. Fail the request instead.

Also re-register BYOK providers when a Copilot token arrives after a failed mint, since they previously stayed unregistered until the next identity change, and make the unregister log say why.

Fixes #339239

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* chat: Reject stale-account tokens and tool model fallback

A Copilot token fetch that finished after an account switch on the same provider was adopted for the new account, which the BYOK token listener could then use to re-enable providers under the wrong account's policy. Check the account identity after the fetch, like the existing provider and enterprise URI checks.

Model-backed tool invocations now use the same strict model resolution as chat requests instead of falling back to the default model.

Fixes #339303

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

commit.message:
agent host: restore Copilot managed-settings diagnostics (#339354)


## Summary

Fix the Copilot snapshot in **Developer: Policy Diagnostics**, which
currently fails with:

```text
Copilot runtime SDK does not expose getManagedSettings()
```

The bundled runtime no longer exports that function. Use the supported
sessionless `client.rpc.managedSettings.resolve()` API instead. The
current SDK/runtime bundle already supports it, so no dependency upgrade
is needed.

- Resolve through the existing host SDK client, forwarding the current
GitHub token and `vscode-agent-host` client identity while retaining the
configured proxy and enterprise endpoint.
- Preserve the account identity, resolved settings, per-source layers,
and runtime diagnostics, including source failures and cached-policy
fallback warnings.
- Retain bounded startup/query deadlines, prevent a late query after
startup times out, and reject results when authentication changes during
resolution. A diagnostics timeout does not stop the shared runtime.
- Remove the obsolete native-export check and temporary process-wide
proxy environment changes.
- Re-enable the previously gated provider diagnostics test, remove its
known-issue entry, and add a model-free end-to-end test for fetched
server policy.
- Document the sessionless scope and the isolated mock-server workflow.

## Scope

This changes diagnostics, not policy enforcement, harness selection, or
existing conversations. It creates no chat session, executes no policy
helper, and does not include session-local client-injected settings.

Normal runtime cache behavior is unchanged. The report preserves
cache/source warnings, but a returned snapshot alone is not proof of a
fresh server fetch or end-to-end enforcement.

## Validation

- Core compilation, targeted hygiene, and whitespace checks passed.
- 508 focused tests passed, with one existing pending test. Coverage
includes token/client identity, proxy and enterprise endpoint
configuration, signed-out resolution, account changes, source warnings,
startup/query timeouts, and shared-client reuse.
- The formerly gated diagnostics test passed against the real bundled
runtime in strict replay.
- A new registered end-to-end test uses the real host/runtime and replay
proxy to verify an actual server-policy request, account identity,
server policy in both the source layer and effective settings, the
resolved bypass restriction, and no model traffic.
- Manual testing in an isolated Code OSS window verified signed-in
device-policy resolution, then a mocked server policy alongside the
existing device policy. The report showed `source: "mixed"`,
`serverManaged: true`, the expected permissions in both locations,
`bypassPermissionsDisabled: true`, and no diagnostics warnings. The
proxy log independently confirmed a successful policy fetch.

The manual server override was cleared afterward. No real device or
enterprise policies, global proxy settings, or certificates were
changed.

*🤖 Authored with GitHub Copilot on behalf of @rwoll.*

commit.message:
mcp: fix customization migration in multi-root workspaces (#339333)

* mcp: fix customization migration in multi-root workspaces

- Same-named `.vscode/mcp.json` servers in other workspace folders are
  never registered because the client resolves duplicate names by
  precedence, so the migration plan never saw the shadowed entries and a
  session scoped to a shadowed folder was offered nothing. Shadowed
  servers are now assessed with their resolved configuration so every
  folder's entries can be offered.
- Each workspace folder migrates into its own `.mcp.json`, so a matching
  server name in another folder cannot overwrite anything. The cross-root
  conflict guard rejected these migrations and asked users to rename
  servers; it is removed, and conflicts within the same destination are
  still rejected.
- Removing the only remaining property of a JSON object left a dangling
  trailing comma. Migrating every server out of a `.vscode/mcp.json` that
  ends with a trailing comma produced invalid JSON, failed verification,
  and was reported as a rollback failure. `setProperty` now removes that
  comma, as it already did for arrays.
- The disabled state of migrated servers was keyed by the session's root
  order rather than the workspace folder index that identifies root
  `.mcp.json` servers, so it could be applied to another folder's server.

Fixes #337097
Fixes #335884

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* mcp: keep same-named server precedence during partial migration

- The session receives the client-forwarded `.vscode/mcp.json` server
  ahead of root `.mcp.json` servers. Migrating only the folder whose
  server takes precedence let a shadowed same-named server in another
  folder take over and silently change the session's configuration.
  Shadowed servers now migrate first, and the server shadowing them only
  migrates once they all have; otherwise it is rejected with guidance to
  migrate them together.
- The settings sync test asserted the invalid `{ , }` output that
  `setProperty` produced when removing the only property before a
  trailing comma, which the previous commit fixed.

(Commit message generated by Copilot)

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

Unify sandbox settings and managed policy presentation (#339058)

* Unify sandbox settings and managed policy presentation

Unify cross-platform sandbox enablement, expose Agent Host sandbox controls, and forward resolved defaults without duplicating SDK fallbacks. Improve settings labels, discoverability, and ordering, and decouple managed policy presentation from the Settings editor.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Keep upcoming sandbox deprecation warnings visible

Enable developer tool access by default, remove local harness wording, and stabilize the Git overlay integration test fixture.

* Address sandbox policy review feedback

Remove legacy session policy metadata and cover replacement and clearing. Clarify sandbox network settings and document all policy restrictions.

Co-authored-by: Copilot <223556219+Copilot@users.noreply.github.com>

* Reconcile restored sandbox settings and persist applied state (#339205)

Resolve saved sandbox choices against current managed policy before notifying providers. Persist confirmed enablement rather than pending or rejected choices, with restore and persistence regression tests.

commit.message:
Fix ExpectNoError and Expect(err).NotTo(HaveOccurred()) anti-pattern in e2e tests (apps)

AI assistance: Codex helped revise assertion explanations with operation and resource context and validate the changes.

kubectl: keep a multi-line event message inside its table row

`kubectl events` writes each event as one tab-separated row into a
tabwriter, passing the message through unchanged. A tabwriter ends a row
at a line break, so an event whose message spans several lines is printed
as extra lines that belong to no event and carry no columns, which breaks
the table.

Event messages are routinely multi-line: an exec probe failure embeds the
probe command's output verbatim, so any probe that prints more than one
line produces one.

The table printer behind `kubectl get events` already cuts a cell at its
first break character and appends "...". Do the same in the events command
so both render the same event the same way.

    ERROR: staging/src/k8s.io/ktesting/format/format.go:95:3: stditerators: NumField/Field loop can simplified using Type.Fields iteration (modernize)

ktesting: update URLs

The new URLs will become live once the next release gets tagged.

ktesting: move to staging

This moves the existing code unchanged, updates package and module name, and
updates all import statements.

ktesting: staging template files

As staging repo some additional files are required.

DRA node allocatable resources: clarify CapacityKey docs

The examples shouldn't be understood as specifying a literal usage of the key -
that would contradict the intended semantic of QualifiedName.

DRA consumable capacity: unambiguous parsing of old allocation result

Theoretically it could have happened that older Kubernetes wrote an allocation
result with capacities that have conflicting names, when a DRA driver published
slices with such a conflict. To avoid randomness in such a case,
"fully-qualified" gets preferred.

DRA consumable capacity: fix allocation result lookup

Two in-tree places looked for entries with a literal string lookup.  This
compared a QualifiedName from a current slice against a QualifiedName from an
allocation result, which is based on some older slice. The literal lookup
breaks if the slices changed from fully-qualified to un-qualified or vice
versa.

The correct approach is to do what lookupAttribute for constraints does: check
both forms. Following the example set by lookupAttribute, fully-qualified is
given precedence in case of a conflict.

DRA CEL: deterministic name conflict resolution

Nothing prevents DRA drivers and users from publishing resp. requesting the
same capacity with and without driver name prefix.

Validation could prevent this for ResourceSlices (driver name is known) but
doesn't. It's probably also not worth doing because DRA drivers are trusted and
can trivially avoid this; validation would just add overhead. Lookup for
constraints resolves this conflict via "fully-qualified wins". CEL lookup was
random (last one in map iteration wins), now it also prefers fully-qualified.

DRA consumable capacity: deterministic name conflict resolution

Nothing prevents DRA drivers and users from publishing resp. requesting the
same capacity with and without driver name prefix.

Validation could prevent this for ResourceSlices (driver name is known) but
doesn't. It's probably also not worth doing because DRA drivers are trusted and
can trivially avoid this; validation would just add overhead. Lookup for
constraints resolves this conflict via "fully-qualified wins". Consumable
capacity resolution was random (last one in map iteration wins), now also
prefers fully-qualified. This is arbitrary, but shouldn't happen in practice.

Validation cannot prevent this for a ResourceClaim capacity request because the
driver name depends on the device under evaluation. This is something that
users could get wrong and the simplistic "prefer fully-qualified" would lead to
surprising results, so instead this is considered an error and causes pod
scheduling to fail if (and only if) it is detected for a device.

DRA consumable capacity: fix capacity name comparisons

When the ResourceClaim requested "driver.example.com/bandwidth" and that DRA
driver published the capacity as "bandwidth", the request failed. Same for the
inverse case.

A less likely problem existed when a DRA driver flipped between publishing with
and without its own driver name as prefix: the allocation result stored
literally what came from the driver at the time of allocation, which then
wouldn't be considered after flipping to the other format.

The fix is to normalize names (drop redundant prefix) before comparing. The
allocation result is written with the same name as in the ResourceSlice,
mimicking the behavior in Kubernetes 1.37. The DRA CPU driver 0.2.0 depends on
that (will be fixed) and Kubernetes 1.37 also did a literal string comparison,
so copying names from the ResourceSlice is required for downgrades.

While at it, the code gets cleaned up a bit:
- Some methods were exported unnecessarily.
- Their parameters can be simplified by passing through a deviceWithID.
  For an exported method that would not be the right API, but internally
  it's fine and simpler.

apiserver: accept large identity header sets with Go 1.27

Go 1.27 rejects requests with more than 500 header values by default
(http.Server.MaxHeaderValueCount, golang/go#79936). Impersonation and
request-header authentication send one header line per group, so a
user with about 500 groups receives HTTP 431 before authentication
runs.

Set MaxHeaderValueCount to 16384 for secure and deprecated insecure
serving: 1 MiB MaxHeaderBytes at about 64 bytes per value (~16 for the
header name and ~48 for the value). This stays bounded while allowing
identities with thousands of groups.

The field is new in Go 1.27, so it is set through setMaxHeaderValueCount,
with a go1.27 build-tagged implementation and a no-op for older Go, so
the change backports to release branches built with Go 1.26.

commit.message:
DRA kubelet plugin: avoid deadlock during shutdown

The shutdown goroutine holds d.mutex while Controller.Stop waits for
the ResourceSlice worker to exit. If HandleError calls PublishResources
at that point, the worker waits for d.mutex while shutdown waits for
the worker.

Read the controller pointer under d.mutex, then release the lock
before calling Controller.Stop.

Document that HandleError may call PublishResources, but must not
call Helper.Stop because it waits for the handler to return.

Add TestStopWhileHandleErrorPublishes to exercise a handler that
calls PublishResources during shutdown and check that both
PublishResources and Helper.Stop return.

commit.message:
docs: remove broken CONTRIBUTING.md link

Signed-off-by: Dane Wanke <info.danewanke@gmail.com>

fix: release startMx with defer in the enriched execStartContainer path

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

fix: execRunPreStart bails out on a canceled context

Same interim narrowing as execStartContainer and execRunPostStart: the
node hangs off the replica's create node, so when that create fails the
pre_start hooks could still fire in the window before errgroup cancels
the context. The structural fix stays tracked in #14081.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

docs: spell out that the ctx.Err() guards narrow the race, not close it

docker-agent's review of the previous commit's fix correctly pointed
out that the ctx.Err() guard added to execStartContainer/execRunPostStart
narrows the race it targets but does not eliminate it: close(done[...])
still runs inside the failing node's own goroutine, strictly before
errgroup's cancel() on that goroutine's returned error. A dependent
unblocked from <-done[dep.ID] can observe ctx.Err() == nil for a brief
window even though its dependency just failed for a genuine reason.

This is exactly the structural gap the epic (#14081) already flagged
in its "failed-dependency semantics" comment before this PR existed:
the real fix carries each node's success/failure through what
dependents wait on (e.g. a chan error) instead of inferring it from
ctx.Err(), uniformly across every operation type - including the
already-merged execCreateHookContainer, which has the same limit.
That is a dedicated brick of the executor lot, not squeezed into this
PR's diff.

No behavior change: this documents the residual window explicitly at
both guard sites and in the regression test, so the next reader (and
the next PR) doesn't mistake "narrows" for "closes".

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

fix: a failed pre_start/start no longer lets its dependent run

A node's done-channel closes strictly before errgroup cancels its
derived context on that same error - the close happens synchronously
inside the failing node's goroutine, ctx cancellation only after it
returns. A dependent blocked in run()'s
select { case <-done[dep.ID]: ...; case <-ctx.Done(): ... } therefore
always sees its dependency's done-channel ready first, regardless of
whether that dependency failed for a genuine reason or was cancelled.

execCreateHookContainer already guarded against exactly this. The two
other new dispatch functions from the previous commit did not:
execStartContainer's enriched branch could call ContainerStart right
after its OpRunPreStart failed for real (e.g. "no hook runner
container found"), contradicting pre_start.go's documented guarantee
that a non-zero hook exit gates service start - and symmetrically for
execRunPostStart after a failed OpStartContainer.

Both now bail out on ctx.Err() first, mirroring the existing guard.
Pinned by a regression test reproducing the race deterministically: no
ContainerStart expectation is registered, so the unguarded code calls
it from inside the errgroup worker goroutine, where gomock's missing-
expectation failure hangs the test binary instead of failing it
cleanly - a stronger tell than a plain assertion failure would have
been.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

feat: executor runs start-phase operations

Wire the plan executor to the start-phase vocabulary the reconciler
already produces (#14200): OpWaitCondition, OpRunPreStart, the enriched
OpStartContainer, and OpRunPostStart all had no case in executeNode
and hit "unknown operation type".

Every operation reuses the exact imperative primitive it mirrors —
waitDependency, runPreStart, runHook, injectSecrets/injectConfigs — so
behavior and events cannot drift between the two engines: execWaitCondition
resolves the dependency's live containers and hands off to the same
polling/condition-check functions waitDependencies uses; the enriched
OpStartContainer resolves its target either from the observed container
or, for a replica the plan itself creates, from the CreateContainer
node's result (the mechanism OpRenameContainer already relies on), then
injects secrets/configs before ContainerStart; OpRunPreStart re-checks
the daemon first so a replica that started in the observe-to-execute
window skips a redundant hook run.

A replica's pre_start/start/post_start chain shares one event group,
reporting a single Starting→Started progression exactly like
startServiceContainer does today — Starting fires specifically at
StartContainer, not at the (silent) pre_start hooks preceding it.
pkg/api/event.go documents this per-resource progression contract.

Still inert in production: create() (executePlan's only caller never
builds a plan with start-phase scope, so none of this runs outside
tests until a later brick in epic #14081 wires a real caller.
EOF
)

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

api: DownOptions.Images becomes a typed ImagePruneMode, validated upfront

The legal values of DownOptions.Images lived in pkg/compose
(image_pruner.go) while the field itself was a bare string in pkg/api,
and the only validation fired inside ImagesToPrune — after down had
already removed the project's containers, leaving the teardown half
done on a typo. The CLI validated its --rmi flag separately, so only
SDK callers were exposed.

ImagePruneMode and its three values now live in pkg/api next to the
field they constrain (type-aliased in pkg/compose for existing
consumers), down() rejects any other value before touching a single
resource, and the CLI check reuses the same definition. A unit test
runs Down with expectation-free mocks: one daemon call would fail it.

Epic #14074, B.6.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

fix(provider): close stdin when an announce write itself fails

docker-agent found that streamImageTo returned a plain error (channel
intact) when the announce write itself failed -- for the success
announce, and for the error announce on a platform-parse/ImageSave
failure. In both cases the provider never received anything to read
and was left blocked on ReadString, while the caller, seeing a plain
error, never closed stdin either -- a deadlock.

Both paths now return streamAbortedError when the announce write
fails, matching the existing mid-stream/close failure handling so the
caller's errors.As check closes stdin and unblocks the provider.

Pinned by two new regression tests using a writer that always errors,
verified by reverting the fix locally and confirming both fail with a
plain error instead of streamAbortedError.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

fix(provider): address review findings on image distribution

Three fixes from glours' review:

- ensureProviderImages now skips a provider service declaring neither
  image: nor build: (legal for a pure resource provider, e.g. one
  backing a remote Amazon RDS instance). Without the guard, such a
  service reached pull with a fabricated "<project>-<service>"
  reference (GetImageNameOrDefault) under source=registry
  (providerImageSource treats Build == nil as registry-authoritative)
  -- a name that was never real. Already reachable through existing
  e2e fixtures (TestDependsOnMultipleProviders' provider1/provider2),
  only a no-op today because the demo pull() short-circuits on an
  unset env var, not because of any guard here.

- localImageFacts now resolves --digest through the manifest-aware
  localContentDigest instead of the raw ImageInspect ID. Under
  BuildKit provenance attestations, the raw ID covers the attestation
  manifest too and changes on every build even when the runnable image
  content didn't (#13636), which would make the provider re-sync on
  every up for no reason -- defeating docs/extension.md's own
  "identity test" contract for --digest. Threads service.Platform
  through from runProviderPull so the resolved manifest matches what
  the provider will actually run.

- streamImageTo now distinguishes a failure before the success
  announce (invalid platform, ImageSave error -- a clean, well-formed
  error line, channel intact) from one after it (the chunked body
  truncated, channel unresynchronizable) via a new streamAbortedError
  type. Only the latter closes stdin; the provider protocol supports
  several sequential get-image requests per pull invocation, and
  closing stdin on a clean pre-stream error was killing any other
  independent request in the same invocation for no reason.

Each fix is pinned by a regression test, verified by reverting the
fix locally and confirming the new test catches it.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

fix(provider): get-service-config resolves a build-only service's image

A service declaring only build: (no image:) answered get-service-config
with an empty "image" field: service.Image is the YAML-declared value,
and compose-go never fills it in for this case (every other caller of
GetImageNameOrDefault in this package exists precisely because of that).
The provider only ever sees this response, never the model compose
builds internally, so an sbx-style provider building its own runtime
image rejected the service outright with "defines no image".

The response now carries the resolved name (api.GetImageNameOrDefault)
instead - the same one the image phase already built and tagged by the
time a provider asks. The build directive itself is cleared before
marshaling: a provider has no builder to run it against, only an image
identity to run.

Pinned by a regression test using the existing fake-provider harness,
verified by ablation to fail on either half of the fix reverted.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

docs(provider), e2e: image distribution documented and exercised

extension.md gains the Image distribution section: invocation contract
(--image/--digest/--created/--source/--policy), the get-image request
and its chunked image-stream answer (zero-chunk terminated, stdin
exclusivity and drain-before-next-answer contract), the two-branch
decision guidance (digest as identity, created as ordering fallback,
reproducible builds caveat), and the support-by-presence metadata
convention is now stated as the general rule. The example provider
implements pull end to end — request, stock chunked reader, hash
recorded at PROVIDER_PULL_MARKER — and the e2e scenario locks the
whole path: up builds the service image and streams it to the provider
under the local verdict, compose pull re-invokes it under the
freshness contract.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

fix(start): a project made only of provider services could not start

startService errored with 'no container to start' whenever the
project-wide container listing came back empty, before the per-service
filtering that lets provider services pass through. A project whose
services are all provider-backed legitimately reaches the start phase
with zero containers. The empty-list error is now softened for
provider services only — a relay container deployed for published
endpoints still goes through the regular start path.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

feat(provider): providers take part in the image phase of up and pull

ensureImagesExists and docker compose pull now give provider-backed
services their turn: compose invokes the provider's pull command with
the image identity and the state of the local daemon cache
(--image/--digest/--created), plus two verdicts compose alone can
compute so providers never re-implement that arbitration:

- --source: the authority for this invocation — local (the daemon's
  image is the desired state: build-only service, pull_policy build,
  or an image the current run just built) or registry (resolve the
  reference upstream — including the CI workflow where build is only
  the recipe used to publish the image consumers pull);
- --policy: missing on the up path (a usable version suffices) or
  always on compose pull (ensure freshness of the authority).

digest/created describe the cache, they are not instructions: the
provider persists them as the bookkeeping keys of what it ingested —
digest as identity test, created as the ordering fallback for backends
that cannot preserve digests. Providers without the metadata block are
skipped: behavior unchanged.

Providers are independent, so their pulls run without fail-fast
cancellation — the first failure no longer kills its siblings mid-run
and mangles their reports into context-canceled noise; every provider
runs to completion and every failure is reported, prefixed by service.
On the pull path the provider phase runs unconditionally — skipping it
because an unrelated service failed to pull would silently leave
provider runtimes stale — and its error is a per-service pull error,
following their exact regime: reported with them, suppressed by
IgnoreFailures. A fatal errgroup error is reported joined with the
accumulated per-service context instead of dropping it. The provider
runs under the root context: the errgroup context is canceled once
Wait returns and would kill the provider process on the spot.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

feat(provider): pull command and get-image protocol for image distribution

Providers opt into image distribution by declaring a pull block in
their metadata — the presence of the command block is the declaration
of support, generalizing the stop precedent. During its pull command a
provider can request the service image from the local daemon with a
get-image message (optionally platform-narrowed); compose answers on
stdin with one image-stream JSON line then the tar as HTTP/1.1 chunked
data (RFC 9112): length-prefixed blocks need no in-band delimiter in
binary data, the zero-length chunk marks a COMPLETE transfer, and any
stock chunked reader consumes it. There is deliberately no trailer nor
final CRLF after the zero chunk — a stock reader stops there without
consuming further bytes, so the next stdin answer starts clean for a
provider requesting several images. An export failure is announced
in-band through the error field so the provider is never left waiting;
a failure after the announce closes the answer channel so the
truncation is observable as EOF mid-chunk instead of a stream nobody
will finish. The stream is exclusive on stdin for its whole duration —
the framing invariant behind the lock.

get-image is scoped to the pull command: emitted during up, down or
stop it is a protocol error rather than served, so an image export can
never stall another lifecycle command.

Message dispatch moves out of executePlugin into handlePluginMessage,
which also keeps the function under the complexity threshold.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

docs(compose): state that a relay-only endpoint also needs an interface-pinned bind

Binding the announced gateway alone restricts by destination address, not
by the interface traffic arrives on, so another bridge can still reach it
by IP. A provider that pins the socket to the relay-link bridge's own
interface (SO_BINDTODEVICE on Linux) keeps the endpoint relay-only.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

fix(compose): share relay-link network removal and state its isolation precisely

Unify the up and down paths on one removal helper that tolerates both
NotFound and Conflict and emits the same progress events as removeNetwork,
build one down op per relay-link network gated on the shared limiter (so
the empty-ops warning is reachable again), and share the label filter.

Reword the isolation claim: the relay-link network is joined by nothing
else, but its gateway is a host address that local containers can still
reach by IP; only a provider binding exclusively that address keeps the
endpoint off loopback and LAN-facing addresses.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

feat(compose): dedicated network for the provider relay link

get-relay-info answers pointed a locally-bound provider at one of the
dependents' own networks: shared infrastructure every other service on
it could also reach, and no more isolated than any project bridge.

Provision a dedicated, internal:true bridge network scoped to that one
provider service instead, created only when the provider itself sends
get-relay-info -- the provider's own declaration that it binds locally,
never for a provider backing a remote resource. The relay container
joins it alongside the dependents' networks it already joins; it is
torn down with the relay on endpoint changes and on down, including
the no-compose-file down path.

The network's lifecycle is hardened against the races a shared,
project-scoped resource runs into:

- a NetworkCreate conflict on the deterministic name re-checks by
  label (not just by name) before adopting the existing network, so a
  genuine name clash with an unrelated, user-declared network fails
  loudly instead of being silently adopted into the relay's isolation
  boundary;
- a NotFound gateway lookup after losing that conflict falls back to
  an unresolved answer instead of propagating the error;
- removeRelayLinkNetwork and ensureRelayLinkNetworksDown both tolerate
  a NetworkRemove conflict from the daemon's asynchronous endpoint
  disconnect, which can race the relay container's own removal;
- ensureRelayLinkNetworksDown accumulates failures with errors.Join
  across every relay-link network of a project instead of aborting on
  the first one, and skips (warn-only) a network that still has active
  endpoints, mirroring removeNetwork's existing tolerance for regular
  project networks.

docs/extension.md documents that the "desktop" network name in the
get-relay-info answer (under Docker Desktop) is an opaque placeholder,
never a real Docker network a provider can inspect or connect to.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

fix: drop dead x-develop/x-initialSync extension handling

compose-go's loader now silently renames both deprecated
x-initialSync and x-develop extensions to their official
initial_sync and develop attributes before compose ever sees them
as extensions, so the legacy lookups and deprecation warnings for
both can no longer be reached. That's why the e2e test asserting on
the x-initialSync warning broke under the bump.

Simplify both lookups to rely on the promoted fields directly, and
rewrite the e2e test to check the legacy attribute still triggers a
real initial sync instead of asserting on an unreachable message.

Signed-off-by: Guillaume Lours <glours@users.noreply.github.com>

fix: share --parallel budget across down's ops and up's log-attach

down's outer ops dispatch bounded only how many ops ran concurrently,
separate from the semaphore already shared by image removal -- a
single network plus --rmi could spend up to 2x the configured
budget. Network and volume removal now share that same semaphore.

up's post-attach log streaming called ContainerInspect directly and
passed no limiter to doLogContainer, unlike `compose logs --follow`'s
equivalent path, so it never shared --parallel's budget either.

The plan executor also held a node's slot for its whole dependency
wait instead of just its own work, and internal/sync/tar.go's file
sync used a hardcoded cap of 16 instead of --parallel.

Signed-off-by: Guillaume Lours <glours@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: bound compose cp's fan-out and panic-safe log slot release

`docker compose cp` fanned out to every matched container through a
bare unbounded errgroup, ignoring --parallel entirely -- the same
class of gap already closed everywhere else in this package. Routed
it through the existing forEachContainerConcurrent helper instead of
a bespoke fan-out.

inspectWithSlot and doLogContainer both release a semaphore slot
early via an explicit call rather than a defer, so a panic between
acquire and that release leaked the slot forever. Guarded both with
a panic-safe release, scoped tightly in doLogContainer so a later
panic in the same function can't trigger a double release.

Signed-off-by: Guillaume Lours <glours@users.noreply.github.com>
Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

fix: close remaining --parallel gaps on down/stop/start

down and stop rebuilt their per-container limiter on every service
visit, so independent services could each spend a full budget
concurrently -- the same leak already fixed on restart. start's
InDependencyOrder call had no concurrency option, leaving every
`up`'s container-start phase fully unbounded. wait.go goes back to
unbounded on purpose: ContainerWait blocks per container
indefinitely, so capping it would serialize waits meant to run
concurrently.

Also extracts the shared per-container fan-out into one helper reused
by restart/down/stop, and dedupes the concurrency-guard test fixtures.

Signed-off-by: Guillaume Lours <glours@users.noreply.github.com>

fix: stop --parallel starving log-follow's monitor or restart's cap

Logs --follow reused the bounded errgroup for both the indefinite log
streams and the monitor goroutine, so once maxConcurrency streams
opened the monitor never started and further services never showed
logs. restart gave each service its own budget, so ready services
could multiply maxConcurrency instead of sharing it.

Bound both with a semaphore that gates only the connect/restart call,
never the indefinite work that follows, sharing one instance across
restart's services. Adds regression tests, plus one guarding the
topological node order a bounded errgroup now relies on in executor.

Signed-off-by: Guillaume Lours <glours@users.noreply.github.com>

fix: honor --parallel across all bulk engine-call fan-outs

errgroup.SetLimit(0) means "allow zero goroutines", not "unlimited",
and maxConcurrency's Go zero-value is 0 — only NewComposeService sets
it to -1 explicitly. Any composeService{} literal built without it
(common in tests) silently deadlocked at every call site that called
SetLimit unconditionally.

Separately, --parallel/COMPOSE_PARALLEL_LIMIT was only ever wired
into pull, push, and the dependency-graph traversal, despite the docs
promising a generic bound on "concurrent engine calls". Every other
bulk operation (kill, pause, down, the up/create plan executor, logs,
ps, top, wait, restart, remove, images, model pulls, watch) launched
one goroutine per container/image/DAG-node with no cap at all.

Fix both via a shared newLimitedErrgroup helper applied at every
fan-out site, threading maxConcurrency through forEachContainerConcurrent
and ImagePruner, which had no access to composeService. Add a
regression test for the zero-value case.

service_containers.go's waitDependencies is intentionally left
unguarded: it's a per-dependency ticker poll, not a burst of engine
calls.

Signed-off-by: Guillaume Lours <glours@users.noreply.github.com>

fix: start lists service containers through getContainers

The start flow hand-rolled its ContainerList without the ConfigHashLabel
presence filter every other listing applies (getDefaultFilters) — the
actual source of pre_start hook runners leaking into startService and
waitDependencies, patched downstream by isNotHookContainer. Routing
through getContainers fixes the leak at the source, like
getContainersByService already does; the isNotHookContainer guards stay
as defense-in-depth.

The dry-run client keyed its ContainerList interception on the calling
function: caller "start" answered from the faked-creations cache, while
caller "getContainers" fell back to the real daemon once the cache was
seeded — so routing start through getContainers made dry-run-created
containers invisible to the start phase ("service has no container to
start", TestUpDryRunMissingImage). The getContainers case now keeps
answering from the seeded cache, where faked creations land.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

fix: address the second round of copilot/docker-agent findings

Five more findings landed on the previous commit (three from a fresh
copilot-pull-request-reviewer pass, two from docker-agent):

- **Duplicate hook containers** (observed_state.go): a runner created
  before the ConfigHashLabel exclusion existed (or by an older compose
  version) still carries that label, so it matches getContainers' own
  filters and is already present in `raw` -- appending getHookContainers'
  result unconditionally classified it twice, scheduling two removals for
  one ID. Deduplicated by container ID before classification. Locked in by
  TestCollectObservedState_LegacyHookRunnerNotDuplicated.

- **Hook runners misjudged as a satisfied dependency** (service_containers.go):
  waitDependencies filtered a dependency's containers the same way
  startService's own replica filter used to (isService + isNotOneOff, no
  hook exclusion) -- a dependency's retained/exited runner could be read as
  the dependency itself, either masking a genuinely missing dependency or
  reporting an unhealthy one that's really just a diagnostic leftover.
  Added isNotHookContainer there too.

- **per_replica bypassing the stale-runner purge** (reconcile.go): the
  early return added for #14259 skipped the purge loop entirely, so
  runners from a prior per_replica: false generation would never be
  cleaned up once a hook switched to per_replica: true. Reordered: the
  purge always runs when there's a service to reconcile; only the create
  loop is skipped for per_replica. Locked in by
  TestReconcileContainers_StaleHookRunnersPurgedEvenWhenPerReplica.

- **keptRunning ignores stops already planned elsewhere** (reconcile.go):
  a replica reported running in the observed-state snapshot but already
  scheduled for a stop by planRecreateNetworks or planStopDependents
  (network recreate, a restart: true dependency cascade) would not
  actually be running by the time the start phase evaluates pre_start --
  but keptRunning didn't know that, so no runner got planned and start
  later failed with "no hook runner container found". Only counts a
  replica as kept when stoppedByPlan has no entry for it. Locked in by
  TestReconcileContainers_HookRunnerPlannedWhenCascadeStopsRunningReplica.

- **Success-removal uses the cancellable ctx** (pre_start.go): inconsistent
  with the cancellation-cleanup path in the same file, which already uses
  context.WithoutCancel to guarantee removal survives a Ctrl-C landing in
  the narrow window right after a hook's success. Matched the pattern.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

fix: address copilot-pull-request-reviewer's 3 findings on the hook-runner plan

A GitHub Copilot PR review (docker/compose#14221#pullrequestreview-5300897216)
found three real issues in the reconciliation-plan-based hook runners, all
confirmed by direct reproduction against a live daemon before being fixed:

- **Hook runners excluded from discovery, stale runners persist.**
  collectObservedState's single getContainers call requires ConfigHashLabel
  (getDefaultFilters), which hook runners deliberately never carry -- so they
  never reached the classification loop that populates HookContainers, and
  planPreStartHookRunners never saw a stale runner to purge. Reproduced: a
  failed hook run followed by a second `up` failed with "container name ...
  already in use" instead of recovering. Fixed by listing hook containers
  separately, by project+hook label alone (new getHookContainers), and
  merging them in before classification. Locked in by a new e2e scenario,
  TestPreStartHookRetryAfterFailureSucceeds, that reproduces the exact
  failure-then-retry sequence.

- **Prepared hook runners misclassified as service replicas.** start's
  containers.filter(isService(name), isNotOneOff) has no reason to exclude a
  hook runner: it carries the same project/service labels as a real replica
  and no one-off label either. Added isNotHookContainer to the filter chain
  in startService, so a hook runner is never counted as (or started as) a
  surviving replica.

- **Per-replica hooks create runners before unsupported configuration is
  rejected.** per_replica is not yet supported (#14259): runPreStart
  validates every hook up front and rejects the whole service before
  executing any of them, but planPreStartHookRunners had no equivalent
  check, so create/up would plan (and leave behind) runners for a service
  whose hooks could never run. Mirrored the same up-front, all-or-nothing
  validation in planPreStartHookRunners.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

feat: reconciliation plan creates pre_start hook runners

pre_start hook containers become first-class resources of the
reconciliation plan. The reconciler plans one OpCreateHookContainer per
declared hook — gated on the same predicate the start phase uses to run
the hooks: a replica to start and no running replica SURVIVING the plan
(a recreated replica is not running at start time, so its runners are
planned too). Runner creation depends on every replica node (the
executor resolves the VolumesFrom target against a final live view),
on the infrastructure, and on the purge of previously observed runners:
names are deterministic (<project>-<service>-pre_start-<i>) so repeated
plans converge on the same container instead of accumulating anonymous
ones, and a new HookIndexLabel ties each runner to its hook.

runPreStart becomes pure execution: it looks up the created-state
runner for each hook by label and never creates one. A declared hook
without a prepared runner is an actionable error naming the
reconciliation command (docker compose up <service>) — the accepted
consequence is that stop-then-start of a hooked service errors, since
runners are consumed on success (locked by e2e). Success removal,
failure retention and cancellation cleanup are unchanged.

Runners stay invisible to the start/ps container listings — they carry
no ConfigHashLabel, which getDefaultFilters requires — and down keeps
removing them by hook label.

Rebased onto main, which diverged substantially since this branch was
opened (the unrelated container-spec-layering refactor, #14093,
restructured compose-go's ServiceConfig/PreStartHook types this PR also
touches). Reconciling pre_start.go/pre_start_test.go against that
refactor surfaced a real bug: createPreStartContainer builds the hook's
config via the shared getCreateConfigs, which unconditionally stamps a
ConfigHashLabel — silently contradicting this same commit's own
"invisible to ps/start" guarantee above, since that label is exactly
what getDefaultFilters requires. Fixed by deleting the label after
getCreateConfigs returns, with a test asserting its absence (an
independent local review, via the GitHub Copilot CLI, and a
fresh-context review agent both converged on catching this during
rebase verification). Also restored two security/label tests that only
existed on one side of the rebase (SecuritySensitiveFieldsHonored,
HookLabelsMerged), ported to call createPreStartContainer directly.

Also addresses glours' three review comments on this PR: hook-container
create operations for a service no longer chain serially (each depends
on the same shared containerNodes+infraDeps+purges set, letting the
executor create them in parallel), the corresponding plan-string test
assertion, and a clearer missing-runner error message hinting this
isn't necessarily a planning bug.

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

feat: reconciler plans the purge of stale pre_start hook runners

pre_start hooks run in ephemeral containers. When a run fails, the
runner is deliberately retained for post-mortem inspection, and the next
run purges it — but that purge lived entirely inside the imperative
primitive, invisible to the reconciliation plan. It is now a plan
operation: when pre_start is going to run again (hooks declared, no
replica running at observation — the imperative gating), the plan emits
one best-effort RemoveContainer per stale runner, dropping its anonymous
volumes, exactly the warn-only semantics of the imperative purge that
remains in place as backstop.

Observed state learns to tell hook containers apart: they carry no
container-number label and previously classified as a service replica
numbered 0. They now land in a dedicated HookContainers bucket the
reconciler plans purges from.

The imperative primitive is also split into its lifecycle-free execution
piece (execPreStartHook: start, wait, log streaming, retain-on-failure)
and the create/remove pieces around it, recomposed identically in
runPreStart — locked by the existing characterization tests. This
prepares moving hook-container creation and post-success removal into
the plan once the start phase lands (#14200).

Signed-off-by: Nicolas De Loof <nicolas.deloof@gmail.com>

fix: report every tagged-image removal failure, not just one

removeTaggedImagesOp switched to a plain errgroup.Group so one
image's failure can't cancel the others still in flight, but
Wait() only ever surfaces the first error returned to it,
silently dropping any other concurrent failures. Aggregate every
failure instead, the same way removeImages already separates
tolerated outcomes (still-in-use, already-gone) from real errors
before joining them.

Also give a tagged-image listing failure its own "Tagged images"
label instead of the generic Compose-wide one, matching the
dedicated label the dangling-image path already has.

Signed-off-by: Guillaume Lours <glours@users.noreply.github.com>

fix: stop one tagged-image failure from starving the rest

removeTaggedImagesOp shared an errgroup.WithContext-derived ctx across
every image removal goroutine. A genuine failure on one image canceled
that ctx, so every image still queued behind it failed with "context
canceled" instead of ever being attempted -- a regression from the
independent per-image ops it replaced.

Also extracts the Conflict/NotFound tolerance rule and the
orphaned-image check into single shared helpers instead of leaving two
independently maintained copies to drift apart, and drops a return
bucket nothing outside its own test consumed.

Signed-off-by: Guillaume Lours <glours@users.noreply.github.com>

fix: stop dropping the still-in-use count on a genuine removal failure

When a dangling-image batch had both a genuine removal error and an
image tolerated as still in use, with nothing actually removed, the
error path reported only the genuine failure and silently dropped the
still-in-use count — the same information loss the "Removed" label
was already fixed to avoid, just on its error-reporting sibling
branch. Both facts now show up together regardless of which path the
batch's outcome takes.

Signed-off-by: Guillaume Lours <glours@users.noreply.github.com>

fix: tolerate a dangling image still in use like every other resource

A dangling image still in use failed the whole op, while a tagged
image or volume in the same state only gets a swallowed warning via
removeResource — same daemon condition, inconsistent outcome. Dangling
images now get the same tolerance. Also stop claiming "Removed" when
a removal failure means nothing actually was, bound the tagged-image
fan-out the same way the dangling one already is, and share the
listing+filter logic between the down and watch paths instead of
duplicating it.

Signed-off-by: Guillaume Lours <glours@users.noreply.github.com>

fix: don't let a tagged-image listing failure abort other down cleanup

Found during review of #14219: `ensureImagesDown` still listed tagged
images to prune synchronously and returned the error immediately,
before `down` had scheduled the already-built network/volume cleanup
ops onto its errgroup — the exact same hazard just fixed for dangling
images, on a different code path. The listing is now deferred to when
its own op runs, so a failure surfaces as a visible error without
blocking sibling ops.

`down --rmi` always printed "Dangling images ... Removed" even when
